column1: # GROUND TRUTH (read straight from zaproxy/action-baseline's actual source,
# action's rules file ONLY understands the action "IGNORE" — it collects
# plugin IDs whose 2nd column is exactly "IGNORE" and uses them to filter
# alerts out of the report. It does NOT support "FAIL"/"WARN" overrides the
# way zap-baseline.py's native -c mechanism does; a "FAIL" line here is
# silently inert (confirmed empirically across several PR canhoto runs
# before finding this in the source — plugins.length stayed 0, so -c was
# never even passed to the container).
# Actual mechanism: zap-baseline.py fails (non-zero exit) if ANY alert at
# WARN-or-above remains after filtering, so the workflow does NOT pass
# `-I` (that would suppress ALL warn-level failures, defeating the gate).
